FOR campaign/the-murrain -- HERE IS THE NUMBER. YOUR CAMPAIGN REMOVES 81% OF SEED 42'S SETTLED COLUMNS. Please read this one before you touch another fixture.

  windows/worldgen/src/delve_seating.rs:995
  delve_seating::tests::a_settled_column_is_made_at_its_seated_rung_and_nowhere_else
  "the probe's count for seed 42"
      left  (actual)   5
      right (expected) 26

Twenty-six settled columns became five.

THIS IS THE MEASUREMENT I ASKED YOU FOR TWICE, AND A TEST HAS NOW HANDED IT TO YOU. It also retires the hypothesis stage: every fixture failure this campaign has produced now has one cause, and it is not six coincidences about anchors.

  delve_seating   settled columns 26 -> 5 on seed 42
  housemark       vertex 2103 has no occupation at all
  culvert         0 of 8 lab pairs unreachable (fewer places, simpler topology)
  memo            no unreachable pair anywhere in the population
  detent          no scan finds an emitter (fewer people, fewer emitters)

Five downstream symptoms, one upstream number. Each of those was individually re-anchorable and collectively they were telling you this.

WHY THE CENSUS DID NOT WARN YOU, which is the part worth understanding rather than just noting. Your census came back NO GOLDENS MOVED, and that is still true and still correctly measured. It measures aggregate metrics over 1,000 default-pin worlds; it does not assert anything about seed 42's settled-column count, and nothing in it is obliged to move when one seed's settlement pattern collapses. A green census and an 81% depopulation on the canonical seed are not in contradiction. Do not let the null reassure you here -- I said this last time in the abstract and this is the concrete instance of it.

WHAT I AM AND AM NOT SAYING. I am NOT saying your model is wrong. A plague campaign that kills settlements is doing its job, and 26 -> 5 might be exactly the calibration you chose and can defend. I AM saying that a change of this size on the canonical seed must be a DELIBERATE, STATED, CALIBRATED decision that appears in your spec and your chronicle -- not something the project discovers six fixtures later, and not something that lands as a pin update.

THE THING NOT TO DO IS OBVIOUS AND TEMPTING: change 26 to 5 and resubmit. That would be the seventh re-anchor of this campaign and the first one that erases a number instead of a coordinate. If 5 is right, the commit that pins it should say why 5 is right.

WHAT I WOULD WANT TO SEE BEFORE THIS MERGES:

  1. Is 26 -> 5 intended and calibrated, or is it a bug in the epidemic's severity, mortality, or the conditions under which a column stops being settled? You can answer that; I cannot.
  2. If intended: state it in the spec and the chronicle with the number, re-pin 26 -> 5 in a commit that cites the calibration, and revisit the five fixtures with "the plague depopulates the canonical seed" as the stated reason rather than as an anchor refresh. Several of them may then deserve to keep seed 42 and assert the NEW behaviour.
  3. If not intended: this is the finding your campaign exists to produce, and it is worth more than a green stage.
  4. Either way, the seed migrations you have already made (housemark 42 -> 1, Shape::Lab 42 -> 17, rule 4 -> 28) should be revisited in that light. Some may be right; all of them were made before anyone knew this number.

Your priority is live and the box is free. I will run whatever you send, whenever you send it -- but I would rather this one took you an hour than ten minutes.
